directions.name: the-room-you-are-standing-in
directions.governingIdea: The site is not a description of the room where the work happens — it IS that room, seen from the doorway, with one light in it, and every element is placed by how far it stands from that light.
directions.singleMindedProposition: Look into the room before you decide: one lamp, one chair, a woman with her coat still on, and a pair of hands that never land.

narrativeSpine.openWound: You have been flattened long enough to start searching at eleven at night, and every page you open wants you to believe something before it will tell you what will happen to your body — so you keep closing tabs on the one question you cannot make yourself type: do I have to take my clothes off.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: The first screen is a doorway into a low-lit room. A woman is sitting in a chair with her coat still on, and a pair of hands is stopped a hand's width above her shoulders. That gap is the loudest thing on the page. What happens in it?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is your own embarrassment, and it wins by default — nobody is going to answer a question you will not ask out loud. What it costs is another eight months of carrying the thing you came in with, while calling it deciding.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: The practitioner enters at the fourth beat as the person who has sat in that room with strangers for years: her own plain sentences at reading scale first, her training in small type underneath, and no borrowed logos, no press awards, no client wall. (Name, years and training are UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 and ship as visibly-marked placeholders until the client confirms.)
staircaseBeats: Root — the doorway. The plate at doorway scale, three flat sentences set into its own unlit quadrant. Dense, close, quiet; the smallest bloom on the site.
Sacral — register change to a near voice and small type: what the hour is like from inside the chair, in a real domestic room, at the scale of someone speaking beside you.
Solar plexus — register change to display verbs. Clearing, charging, repairing, restructuring, set as four words with the light widening a step behind each.
Heart — register change to a face and a hand-set paragraph at reading measure. The practitioner, empathy before credentials.
Throat — register change to the coldest, plainest block on the page: what this is not, set on the unlit surface with no bloom behind it at all. The one region the light does not reach.
Third eye — register change back to warmth and to one named person: a single before-and-after paragraph, no adjectives.
Products — register change to a schedule. Real dates, real prices, tabular figures, three offering kinds at equal billing, lit by the widest bloom yet.
Crown — the light is now the entire viewport and the composition opens all the way: one sentence, one control, nothing else.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: someone who has had an appointment window open in another tab since March and has never got as far as the contact form, because the thing she needs to know is the thing she cannot make herself ask. After: someone who has spent an hour in a chair with her coat on the back of it, who knows exactly what did and did not happen to her, and who has an opinion about it instead of a fear. Nothing was cured. The not-knowing was.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The crown answers the gap the doorway opened, in the words the doorway used: the hands never land. Beneath it sits one control — Ask for a time — and the confirmation that follows states the held hour plainly and says a person will reply, because a person does.

directions.name: the-answer-printed-first
directions.governingIdea: The site's first act is to remove an embarrassment, so the design's first act is to make that removal impossible to miss: the answer is printed before the question is asked, at the size of a headline, with nothing standing in front of it.
directions.singleMindedProposition: You stay dressed, nobody touches you, and nothing is asked of your beliefs — printed first, at full size, before anything at all is sold.

narrativeSpine.openWound: The thing you actually need to know is whether a stranger will ask you to undress and then touch you, and it is precisely the thing you cannot type into a contact form — so you read six sites about energy and none about your body, and you close all six.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: Three sentences fill the first screen and every one of them is about what will NOT happen. Underneath, in small type, the obvious question comes back: so what DOES happen, for an hour?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is the FAQ — this category's habit of filing the only answer that matters two clicks in, where it is found by people who had already decided to book. What it costs is the sceptical, curious adult who leaves believing that nobody was ever going to say.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She arrives at the fourth beat in exactly the same flat register: no adjectives, no mission statement, no borrowed authority. A person who describes what she does and declines to say what it will do for you. (Name, years and training UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 — marked placeholders until confirmed.)
staircaseBeats: Root — three sentences at 88px and nothing else in the viewport. No picture, no eyebrow, no navigation flourish, no tint.
Sacral — the register drops hard to 18px reading measure and second person: what the hour is like, minute by ordinary minute.
Solar plexus — register change to the page's only numbered list: the four verbs, set as four items and nothing more.
Heart — register change to a photograph, finally, at full width and full stop, with the practitioner's paragraph set BENEATH it rather than over it.
Throat — register change to the one shaded region on the site: what this is not, hard-ruled, in the same flat sentences as the opening.
Third eye — register change to a single long paragraph at wide measure. One person, before and after, no list.
Products — register change to figures: dates and prices in tabular numerals, rule-separated rows, three kinds at equal billing, not one card.
Crown — the register returns exactly to the opening: same face, same 88px, one sentence more than there was at the top.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a 51-year-old who has read the word energy forty times this week and still does not know whether she will be asked to lie on a table in a gown. After: someone who can repeat three facts about the hour to her sister without being embarrassed, and who asked for a Tuesday because the price was on the page and she did not have to email to find it.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The crown is literally the fourth sentence of the opening paragraph, set at the same size in the same face: “You stay dressed. Nobody touches you. Nothing is asked of your beliefs. Here is when she is free.” The dates sit directly beneath it, and the request is one screen away.

directions.name: long-dusk-ascent
directions.governingIdea: The page is a single hour of failing light run in reverse: the visitor lands at the darkest point of the brand and physically travels to the lightest, so the root-to-crown climb is made of the page's own material rather than illustrated on top of it.
directions.singleMindedProposition: Start where you are — in the dark, embarrassed — and arrive somewhere brighter by the time you reach the ask.

narrativeSpine.openWound: It is late, the room you are in is dark, and you have been reading about a thing you half-want and half-expect to be humiliated by. The first thing you need is not inspiration. It is to be told what happens to your body, by someone who is not going to be embarrassed telling you.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: You land at the deepest, most enclosed point of the whole site — and within one screen of scrolling the ground under the text is visibly, measurably lighter than it was. It is still moving. Where does it stop?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is the flat page — a single unchanging cream ground that has no direction of travel, so a visitor cannot feel progress and reads the seven things she is told as seven unrelated boxes. What is lost is the arc: the sense that this hour would move her somewhere.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters at the Heart beat, at the exact point where the ground has climbed far enough that a photograph of a person is legible on it — empathy first, in a paragraph of her own words; the training beneath, small. (Name, years, training UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 — marked placeholders.)
staircaseBeats: Root — plum-900 #1E0A1C, the deepest value on the site, dense type, the plate needing no treatment at all because the ground beneath it is already the plate's own darkness.
Sacral — register change to a warmer, closer voice as the ground lifts its first measured step; the last fully-dark plate on the page.
Solar plexus — register change to structure: the four verbs set as the page's only stepped list, the ground now unmistakably mid-value.
Heart — register change to a human face and a first-person paragraph, at the height where the ground can carry a portrait.

Throat — register change to the crossover seam itself. What this is not, set at the ~120px band where the two zones blend — contrast-computed rather than kept clear of type, so the honesty beat sits at the page's turning point.
Third eye — register change into the light half: one before-and-after paragraph on a near-blush ground, type opening as the optical size dials up.
Products — register change to a schedule set on light: dates as headers, prices in tabular figures, three kinds at equal billing.
Crown — blush #FBF3F1, the brightest area on the site, aura-radiant-portrait, and the request.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a woman who has spent four months reading about this at night with the lights off, and has told nobody. After: a woman who told her husband about it over dinner, in ordinary words, because she now has ordinary words for it — she knows what happens, what does not, what it costs and when it is.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The ground stops climbing at the crown, and that is the answer to where it was going: the brightest region on the site is the ask. The line above the form names what the light was — the hour after — and the CTA is the page's only element that sits on pure blush.

directions.name: the-hour-logged
directions.governingIdea: A practitioner with no institutional logos to borrow buys credibility with a record, not a claim — so the site is built as a kept log of one hour, with a measured time-scale down the margin and every passage pinned at the minute it describes.
directions.singleMindedProposition: Here is the hour, minute by minute, written down — decide from the record rather than from the promise.

narrativeSpine.openWound: You cannot tell a serious practitioner from a hobbyist, because they all write the same paragraph about energy and none of them will tell you what physically occurs between the moment you arrive and the moment you leave. So you have no way to judge, and judging is the only thing you are trying to do.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: The margin scale starts at 00:00 and the first mark is annotated: you keep your coat on the back of the chair. Sixty marks are visible down the page. Most of them are still empty — what fills them?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is the unfalsifiable claim: language so general that nothing could ever contradict it, which is comfortable for the practitioner and useless to you. What it costs is your ability to decide at all, so you don't, and it stays open in a tab.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters at the 34-minute mark, where the log records what she is doing rather than who she is — and the paragraph beneath is hers, in her own plain words, empathy before qualification. (Name, years and training UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 — visibly-marked placeholders.)
staircaseBeats: Root — 00:00 to 04:00, the densest cluster of marks on the page. Arrival: coat, chair, clothes, distance. The scale is at its tightest here and the annotations are at their plainest.

Sacral — register change from log to first-person recollection: what the next ten minutes are like from inside the chair, set at reading measure across the wide column while the scale keeps ticking beside it.
Solar plexus — register change to instrument operations: clearing, charging, repairing, restructuring, each pinned at its minute with a hairline leader out to the scale.
Heart — register change to a photograph and a paragraph. The practitioner, at the point in the hour where she is doing the most and saying the least.

Throat — register change to a boxed marginal note in the register of a correction notice: what this is NOT, what is not being claimed, and the complementary-not-a-substitute statement, set as a permanent annotation on the record rather than as a disclaimer at the bottom.
Third eye — register change to prose at wide measure with the scale falling silent for the first time: one person, before and after.
Products — register change to a second scale: the same tabular treatment applied to real dates and prices, three kinds at equal billing, aligned on their digits.
Crown — 60:00. The only mark on the page annotated with a question rather than a description.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a man who has spent two months unable to tell whether this is a serious practice or someone with a website, because nothing he has read could be checked against anything. After: someone who has been through the hour once, has an accurate account of it, and can tell a friend precisely what happened in the order it happened — including the parts that did nothing for him.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The last mark, 60:00, is the only annotation on the record that is a question instead of a description — “when are you free?” — and the live free-slot picker is what fills it. The log that began by telling you your coat stays on ends by asking for a time, in the same numerals.

directions.name: one-lamp-amber
directions.governingIdea: Certainty reads as the absence of persuasion, so the interface gives up its own colour entirely — one warm hue on deep brown and nothing else — in order that the only magenta a visitor ever sees is the light inside the practitioner's own photographs.
directions.singleMindedProposition: Nothing here is trying to convince you; the only bright thing on the page is the work itself.

narrativeSpine.openWound: You have been sold to all week by people who use the word journey, and you are so tired of being persuaded that you have started distrusting warmth itself — which is a problem, because the thing you are actually looking for is a quiet person who will not make a fuss of you.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: Everything on this page is one colour. Then a photograph arrives and it is full of gold and magenta light. Why is that the only colour in the entire place?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is the outcome-adjective list — Confident, Happy, Calm, Relaxed, Loved, Safe — a promise wearing a word cloud, which is both the category's habit and, under the CAP Code, its legal exposure. What it costs you is the ability to believe anything on any of these sites.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters late and small: one paragraph at reading measure, on the same brown as everything else, saying what she does and declining to say what it will do for you. No portrait retouched into the palette, no credential wall. (Name, years, training UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 — marked placeholders.)
staircaseBeats: Root — the tightest, lowest-contrast setting on the site: the three facts in amber on brown, close-set, at the pace of someone speaking carefully.
Sacral — register change to the FIRST plate, full-height and ungraded, arriving after a screen of amber-on-brown with all of its gold and magenta intact. The shock of colour is the whole beat.
Solar plexus — register change back to type-only. Four verbs, one line each, no list markers, no rules.
Heart — register change to a paragraph in the first person at wide measure. The quietest thing on the page.
Throat — register change to a hard stop: what this is not, set as the shortest section on the site, with more air above and below it than anything else has.
Third eye — register change to one before-and-after paragraph, still amber, still one column.
Products — register change to figures: dates and prices in amber tabular numerals with a 2px gold underline as the only rule in the system.
Crown — aura-radiant-portrait full-height, the single brightest frame on the site, with the one solid gold control beneath it.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: someone who has developed an allergy to wellness language and therefore cannot get to anything real underneath it, and who has decided that anyone this warm is probably selling something. After: someone who spent an hour in a low-lit room with a person who did not once tell her how she would feel afterwards, and who found that more convincing than any of it.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The last plate is a face lifted into light and the only coloured control on the entire site sits directly under it: Ask for a time. The colour was never withheld — it was being saved for the work, and the CTA is the first moment the interface allows itself any.

No plum. This is a deep warm BROWN and the distance from the brand's own plum is deliberate — it is also the distance from Othership's #372338
No elevation, no shadow, no second accent, no motion beyond a focus ring: motion_intensity is 1 and literally nothing moves

directions.name: the-mark-is-the-grid
directions.governingIdea: The client already owns the strongest structural idea she has and it is sitting unused inside her own logo — concentric light running outward from a centre — so the mark is promoted from something placed in a header to the layout system the whole site is composed on.
directions.singleMindedProposition: You can crop the logo out of a screenshot of this site and still know exactly whose it is.

narrativeSpine.openWound: Everything in this category looks like everything else in this category, so when you finally find someone you might trust you have no way to tell whether she is different or just better at the same template — and the one thing you are trying to judge is whether this particular person is serious.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: Every edge on this page is part of a circle whose centre is somewhere off the side of the screen. The arcs keep implying it. Where is the centre?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is the platform's own composition — Wix strips, Elementor blocks, Squarespace sections — a vertical stack of full-width bands that makes every practitioner's site the same shape regardless of who she is. What is lost is any way for a real practice to look like itself.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters inside a circle of her own, at the same radius as the first plate — a portrait masked to the mark's geometry with her paragraph set on the arc beneath it, empathy first, training in the small ring below. (Name, years, training UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 — marked placeholders.)
staircaseBeats: Root — the smallest aperture on the site: aura-two-people masked to a 480px circle with the three reassuring sentences set on an arc struck from the SAME centre as the field in the photograph.
Sacral — register change to a wide, low band of type running tangent to a much larger arc; the circle is bigger and now mostly off-screen.
Solar plexus — register change to four small concentric rings, one per verb, the only place in the composition where circles repeat rather than nest.
Heart — register change to a face inside a circle and prose set on its arc.

Throat — register change to the ONE rectangle on the entire site: aura-field-abstract full-bleed at the Beat 3/4 hinge, carrying what this is not. The single break in the geometry is the detail that rewards attention.
Third eye — register change back to circular, larger again, a single before-and-after paragraph at the centre of an open ring.
Products — register change to nested arcs rather than a row of cards: three offering kinds at equal billing as three concentric bands, dates and prices set along them.
Crown — the arc finally closes: the first complete circle on the site, with the request at its centre.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a woman who has opened eleven practitioner sites this month and cannot remember one of them apart from the other, and has concluded that this whole field is interchangeable. After: someone who describes it to a friend as “the one with the rings”, and who books because she could tell the difference between one practice and the next — which turned out to be the thing she had actually been trying to do.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: At the Crown the circle completes for the first and only time, and the request form sits at its exact centre. The centre the arcs have been implying since the first screen turns out to be the visitor: the field runs outward from where she is sitting.

directions.name: the-refusal-column
directions.governingIdea: This practice earns belief by subtraction, so every claim on the site is delivered attached to its own limit: the page is set as two aligned columns — what does not happen beside what does — and the argument is what survives the subtraction.
directions.singleMindedProposition: Here is everything this is not. What is left is an hour, on a date, at a price.

narrativeSpine.openWound: You have read “heal your life” so many times that you now discount everything anyone in this field says, including the true parts — and somewhere under all that discounting is a genuine, unglamorous problem you have been carrying since your mother died, which nobody has offered to simply sit with.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: The left-hand column is much longer than the right-hand one: there are far more things this work is not than things it is. Does anything survive the subtraction at all?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is overclaim, and it is not abstract — three of six researched sites make a claim that would need clinical substantiation, and two ASA rulings are already on the record. What it costs you is that you cannot tell the honest practitioners from the rest, so you treat all of them the same and see none of them.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters in the right-hand column only, opposite a left column that lists what she is not qualified to do — and the pairing is the introduction: the limits are hers, stated by her, first. (Name, years, training UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 — marked placeholders, and the admin's editor carries the permanent CAP reminder beside them.)
staircaseBeats: Root — the widest left column on the page. You do not undress · nobody touches you · nothing is asked of your beliefs — set against a short right column: you sit in a chair, in your own clothes, for an hour.
Sacral — register change: the left column falls to a single line and the right opens into continuous prose about what the hour is actually like.
Solar plexus — register change to the four verbs in the right column, each opposite what it is not, so the method is defined by its boundary.
Heart — register change to a photograph spanning both columns for the first time; the practitioner's paragraph beneath it, in the right column, with her limits opposite.

Throat — register change to the page's structural climax, where the two columns are exactly equal in width for the only time: not therapy, not medicine, not a replacement for either, and the complementary-not-a-substitute statement in full.
Third eye — register change as the left column thins to nothing: one before-and-after paragraph running unopposed at wide measure.
Products — register change to figures: real dates and prices in the right column, with the left carrying only the honest inline caveats (places available, not a live seat count).
Crown — one column. One sentence and one control, where two columns used to be.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a man of 58 who tells people he is fine and has been fine for two years, and who has an unopened bereavement-support leaflet in a drawer because accepting help would mean admitting there is something to help with. After: someone who booked an hour with a person who told him plainly that she could not fix any of it, and found that the only offer in the whole category he could accept.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: By the Crown the left column has run out — there is nothing left to refuse — and one column remains: a single sentence and a date field. What survived the subtraction is exactly what beat 1 said it would be: an hour, in your own clothes, on a day, at a price you can read.
narrativeSpine.loopMechanics: R-1: the opening question (does anything survive?) is paid off structurally, not verbally — the two columns literally converge to one at the CTA, so the answer is visible before it is read.

interfaceCraftEmphasis: I-6 affordance legibility with GUARDED destruction: the pairing pattern is reused as the admin's confirm-guard vocabulary — the irreversible act on the right, exactly what it will do on the left (send to n recipients; delete this document, which 2 issues reference)
I-2 one primary action per screen with its consequence stated beside it rather than after it — publish, send, decline and delete each carry their limit in the adjacent column
I-1 state-completeness including the reference view before deletion (brief §12 — she can see what would break), which is this direction's pairing pattern doing real operational work
excludes: No claim without its limit. Any sentence on the site that would sit in the right column with an empty left column does not ship
No named medical condition and no treat / cure / diagnose / prevent / alleviate verb, physical or psychological — this is a CAP position, not a style preference
No testimonial wall and no borrowed authority: a sole operator cannot borrow spa residencies and Nike logos, and this direction refuses the substitute rather than faking it
No cream or ivory ground — the mid-value warm ash is what keeps a page of refusals from reading as either clinical white or spa-soft
No soft-focus imagery and no euphemism: “you'll be completely comfortable” is not a refusal, it is a soothing adjective standing where a fact should be
directions.layoutArchetype: Two aligned columns read as a pair — the left states what does not happen and what is not promised, the right states what does — line against line down the document, the left narrowing and the right widening as the argument climbs, until a single column remains at the close.
directions.signatureMove: The antiphonal pair: every statement on the site has a limit set on the same baseline beside it, and the two columns converge across the scroll — the refusal column narrowing beat by beat until, at the call to action, only one column is left.
directions.toneRegister: candid argument — unsentimental, generous, earning belief by subtraction
visualToneIndicators: a mid-value warm ash ground with the right column raised onto a lighter surface — the refusals sit down in the page, the offers sit up out of it
an editorial serif with a real italic: the left column is set in italic throughout and the right in roman, so voice is carried by cut rather than by colour
one hairline vertical rule between the columns, at exactly the SC 1.4.11 floor, and no other rule in the system
0px radius; no shadow except the single step that lifts the right column
comfortable density at a strict measure — neither column ever exceeds 62 characters
directions.theUnaskedQuestionAnswer: It is answered as the site's first refusal pair, and it is the widest left column on the page: “You do not undress · nobody touches you · nothing is asked of your beliefs” set line-against-line with “you sit in a chair, in your own clothes, for an hour”. The fear is disarmed by being answered in the same grammar as everything else, which tells the visitor this is simply how this practice talks.
directions.ascentMechanic: structural convergence — the left column's measure narrows and the right's widens by a fixed step per beat, so the composition visibly opens as the argument climbs and resolves to a single column at the Crown

directions.name: fixed-band-editable-field
directions.governingIdea: The product's load-bearing rule is configurable content inside a fixed structure, so the design makes that rule VISIBLE: a permanent dark band is the part nobody can change and the light field beside it is the part she can, on the public site, in the admin and in every mailed issue.
directions.singleMindedProposition: One structure she learns once and then recognises everywhere — so the design cannot decay in month two and the visitor never meets a foreign body.

narrativeSpine.openWound: You arrive on a practitioner's site, read something that almost persuades you, click Book — and land in something that is visibly a different piece of software, in a different typeface, with a different idea of a corner radius. The seam tells you nobody is really in charge here, at the exact moment you were deciding whether to trust someone.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: The dark band down the side has said the same three things since you arrived, and it has not moved once while everything beside it has changed. What is it eventually going to ask you for?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is the stitch — Squarespace plus Acuity plus Eventbrite plus Mailchimp, four registers and four logins bolted together, measured in this category as a visible foreign body every single time. What it costs is the practitioner's credibility at the exact moment of the ask, and it costs her evenings maintaining four things.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters in the light field at the Heart beat, in editable content — which is the point: the band that never changes carries the promise, and the woman who can change her own words is beside it. (Name, years, training UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 — marked placeholders.)
staircaseBeats: Root — the band is at its widest and carries a tall plate with the three facts over it; the light field beside it holds one short paragraph. The fixed part is bigger than the editable part, once, at the top.
Sacral — register change: the field opens into continuous prose and the band narrows a step, holding only the reassurance line and the mark.
Solar plexus — register change to structure in the field: the four verbs, spaced, while the band shows the first date in the diary.
Heart — register change to a portrait and a paragraph in the field, both owner-editable; the band goes quiet.

Throat — register change to the field's only shaded block: what this is not, in the field because she must be able to edit it, with the permanent CAP reminder rendered beside it in the admin's mirror of this exact composition.
Third eye — register change to one before-and-after paragraph at the field's widest measure; the band is now a hairline.
Products — register change to figures rendered live from the Offering records: dates and prices, three kinds at equal billing, in the field, with no second edit needed to publish one.
Crown — the band widens once more and becomes the form: the fixed structure is what does the asking.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a practitioner who has not published a workshop since January because doing it means logging into two systems and she is not sure which one owns the date — and a visitor who can feel that hesitation in the gaps on the page. After: an owner who published a dated, priced workshop in four minutes on a Sunday and watched it appear on the public page with no second edit, and a visitor who never once left one design.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: At the Crown the band widens into the request form and asks for exactly three things — a name, an email, and a time that suits you. The thing that never changed all the way down the page turns out to be the promise it opened with: nothing else is ever asked of you, and the person who replies is the person who wrote every word in the field.

I-6 affordance legibility from the colour-zone rule — gold only ever appears on the band, magenta-deep only ever in the field, so the palette is self-policing and neither colour is ever asked to work on the ground where it fails
I-1 state-completeness across BOTH zones: a band with no counts and a field with no rows are two different empty states and both are designed

No separate newsletter template design — the issue is the same band and field, so there is no way to send something off-brand
directions.layoutArchetype: A permanent dark vertical band of identity and navigation beside a light reading field, present unchanged across the public site, the owner's admin and the mailed issue: the band is the part nobody can edit and the field is the part she can, so the product's fixed-versus-configurable rule is visible at a glance.
directions.signatureMove: One structure, three surfaces: the same dark band and light field carries the public page, the admin and the newsletter — so the owner learns the product once, and the visitor never crosses a seam between the site and the thing that takes her booking.
directions.toneRegister: operable warmth — structured, legible, built to be run by one person
visualToneIndicators: 8px radius on light-field cards and 0px in the band: the radius itself tells you which zone you are in
three warm-tinted elevation levels in the field and ZERO in the band, which is flat by definition because it is a ground and not a surface
a body face designed for maximum character disambiguation, chosen for the 35–65 audience and the reading-glasses-elsewhere note
the band collapses to a top strip under 768px without changing which colour lives where
every screen carries both a large dark image and a bright legible reading surface at the same time
directions.theUnaskedQuestionAnswer: The band answers it and then never stops answering it. The three facts are set in the fixed band at the Root, over the tall plate — and the reassurance line stays in the band at every scroll position and on every interior page, so the answer is CHROME rather than content. A visitor who lands on a workshop detail page from a search result still gets it.

directions.name: no-seam-nightfield
directions.governingIdea: The practice's competence is the product a sceptic can actually verify, so the working machinery leads the design language: the merged calendar, the free-slot picker and the self-expiring hold are one instrument, and the public page is that instrument's face.
directions.singleMindedProposition: There are real free times on her calendar tonight, and the thing that shows them to you was built by the same person who will answer.

narrativeSpine.openWound: You cannot judge whether someone is a serious practitioner or a person with a website, and the only evidence you are given is adjectives. Meanwhile the actual practical questions — what does it cost, when is she free, how long does it take — are all behind a form, which reads as evasive to exactly the sort of person who checks.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: Every price, every duration and every date on this page is already there without asking anyone, and some of the times on it are tonight. Who is on the other end of that?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is enquiry-gated pricing and the client-rendered schedule — half the researched category publishes no price at all, and one studio's booking page returns “No results found” to a static fetch, so its dates do not exist for a crawler, a slow connection or a screen reader. What it costs is the visitor who wanted to check before committing, which is the only visitor this practice can afford to lose.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters as the person visibly attached to the machine: a small portrait beside the response commitment, and one paragraph in her own words. Her authority here is that the calendar in front of you is hers and it is accurate. (Name, years, training UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 — marked placeholders.)
staircaseBeats: Root — the densest, tightest block of rows on the site: the three facts set as three declarative rows with a gradient hairline down their left edge, above the fold, before any picture.
Sacral — register change, hard: one plate at 100vw and full viewport height, uninterrupted, no type on it. Warmth arrives in a single sustained dose after precision.
Solar plexus — register change back to rows: four verbs as four labelled operations with what each one is doing to the field.
Heart — register change to a portrait inset in a 1px frame with a paragraph at reading measure — the only place on the page where the type relaxes.
Throat — register change to an unlit block: what this is not, set with the achromatic border and no gradient hairline anywhere near it. The one region colour does not mark.
Third eye — register change to prose at wide measure, one person, before and after.

Products — register change to the instrument at full strength: real dates as headers, times as standalone tappable objects, prices in tabular figures, three kinds at equal billing, all server-rendered in the initial HTML.
Crown — the free-slot picker itself, live, with tonight on it.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a project manager of 44 who checks everything and has therefore booked nothing, because every site in this field asked her to make contact before it would tell her a price, and she reads that as something to hide. After: someone who picked a Thursday at 6pm off a real calendar, got told plainly that it was held rather than booked for 48 hours, and got a reply from a human the next morning — and whose first thought was that this person is organised.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The last row on the page is a real time on a real day, and requesting it holds that time for 48 hours and says so on the confirmation, in the same numerals — held, not booked, until she replies, and a person does reply. The instrument the page opened with turns out to have been attached to a human being the whole way down.

interfaceCraftEmphasis: I-5 density done right at the highest setting in the set — the merged calendar is the centre of gravity and the data-ink discipline means confirmed bookings, pending holds, derived session blocks and personal blocks are distinguishable at a glance with no decorative chrome competing
I-1 state-completeness as the defining lever: the empty calendar of a new practitioner, a densely booked week, and a day with an expired hold on it are three separately-composed states, per brief §11
I-3 scan hierarchy with tabular figures everywhere a time, price or count appears — nothing about a date is ever ambiguous, and free time is legible AS free

I-6 affordance legibility with a hard rule: the aesthetically tempting hairline #2A222B measures 1.27:1 and is permitted only between non-interactive regions — every input, control and focus boundary uses #7E7182 at 4.27:1
excludes: No third-party widget in a foreign register anywhere in the product — the slot picker, the calendar and the mailed issue are the same design system as the landing page or the concept is void
No enquiry-gated price and no “from” price: every offering's fee is a fact stated on the listing, not a badge and not a conversation
No date that exists only after JavaScript — every date, time and price is in the initial HTML; a client fetch may refresh live availability but must never be what puts the date on the page
No plum ground and no condensed display face: this is a near-black with a plum bias precisely so it is not Othership's #372338 in a technical costume
No decorative colour: one gradient hairline marks whichever region is live and everything else is achromatic, so colour always means something
directions.layoutArchetype: A compact instrument shell of rule-separated rows set in tabular figures at a tight rhythm, one gradient hairline marking whichever region is live, everything else achromatic — slot picker, merged calendar and mailed issue built from the same rows as the public page.
directions.signatureMove: The gradient hairline: a single 1px gold→magenta rule that marks whichever region is live — the selected slot, the active calendar day, the row that needs her today — and is the only chromatic element in an otherwise achromatic instrument, so colour on this site always means something is happening.
directions.toneRegister: nocturnal instrument — precise, competent, warm only at the edges
visualToneIndicators: 3px radius on inputs and cards, 0px on the calendar grid because a dense time grid reads faster square
1px borders and zero shadow at every elevation — the cockpit convention
tabular figures everywhere a time, a price or a count appears
the imagery ratio inverts by surface: small 3:2 insets in a 1px frame on the admin, one plate per beat at full viewport height on the public site
16px body minimum at 1.6 — the legibility floor is respected even in the densest direction of the ten
directions.theUnaskedQuestionAnswer: It is answered as three DATA ROWS, in the same rule-separated format as a price or a duration — clothing: your own · contact: none · belief: not required — set above the fold before any photograph. The fear is disarmed by being demoted to a specification: it is a fact about the service, filed with the other facts about the service, and that flatness is the reassurance.
directions.ascentMechanic: rhythm and openness — the row rhythm starts at its tightest and the rules space out step by step, so the instrument literally relaxes as the page climbs and the crown is a single wide row

directions.name: plate-sequence-captioned
directions.governingIdea: Six commissioned plates are an unusually strong asset for a sole practitioner, so the site is built as a photo essay in which every picture is captioned and therefore makes a claim — photography used as evidence rather than as atmosphere.
directions.singleMindedProposition: Look at what actually happens, in order, with someone telling you plainly what you are looking at.

narrativeSpine.openWound: You have looked at forty pictures of candles, crystals and empty treatment rooms this week and not one of them showed you a person having the thing done to them — so you still do not know what it looks like, and what you cannot picture, you cannot agree to.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: The first plate is captioned like evidence: she is dressed, her coat is on the chair, the hands are twenty centimetres above her shoulders, nothing is touching her. The captions keep counting down the page. What is the last picture?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is photography with nothing asked of it — soft-focus interiors placed behind a headline to set a mood, which is the measured imagery default of this entire category. What it costs is the one medium that could have answered a procedural question faster than any sentence, spent instead on atmosphere.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters as a photograph with a caption in the third person and a paragraph in the first — a real named human with a face, before any explanation of the modality, empathy first and training after. (Name, years, training UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 — marked placeholders.)
staircaseBeats: Root — aura-two-people at 100vw, the first thing on the site, with a caption that states what is in the frame and what is not touching whom.
Sacral — register change from caption to prose: a passage at reading measure on the pale ground with no image at all, so the eye rests before the next plate.
Solar plexus — register change to a plate with FOUR captions, one per verb, keyed to regions of the same image — the only annotated frame on the site.
Heart — register change to a portrait and a first-person paragraph, the caption in her own voice for the only time.
Throat — register change to aura-field-abstract, the one non-figurative plate, as a deliberate pause: a picture of nobody, captioned with what the work is not.
Third eye — register change to the widest measure on the site with no picture, one person, before and after.
Products — register change to figures beneath a plate: real dates and prices, three kinds at equal billing, in the same caption typography as the photographs.
Crown — aura-radiant-portrait at full viewport, the brightest frame in the sequence, its caption the last line of the essay.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a woman who cannot picture the thing and therefore keeps postponing it, and who has quietly assumed it involves a table, a gown and someone's hands on her back. After: someone who has seen exactly what the hour looks like before she agreed to it, sat through it in her own coat, and afterwards described it to her daughter as much more ordinary than she expected.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The last plate is a face lifted into the light and its caption is the only one written in the second person — the end of an hour, in her own clothes, nothing having touched her. The request form is set directly beneath it, so the question the first caption opened is closed by the last picture rather than by a sentence.

one soft under-image shadow so a full-bleed plate lifts fractionally off the pale ground, and no other elevation exists

directions.name: the-surveyed-field
directions.governingIdea: Fifteen years in the same field means she could draw it from memory, so the site IS that drawing — a survey of a field of light, contour rings measured off the real centre of each photograph, in which every ring breaks open wherever a word meets it, because on a real survey the line always yields to the label.
directions.singleMindedProposition: Someone has been here often enough to draw the map, and she has printed the key.

narrativeSpine.openWound: You have opened eleven of these pages this month and every one of them told you how it would make you FEEL and not one of them told you what would be DONE — so you are trying to tell a serious practice from a nice-sounding one using only the pictures, at eleven at night, without being able to ask the one question you actually have.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: Every plate on this page has rings drawn over it, tightening toward one point, each ring carrying a small measured figure. Something is being surveyed. The tightest ring on the whole site is the first thing you read. What is at its centre?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is the category's habit of asserting instead of showing — a field in which the benefit is always described and the procedure never is, so a sceptical adult has no way to separate fifteen years of practice from six weeks of a certificate. What is lost is the person who would have come and could not tell.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters as the surveyor: hers is the one plate whose rings are struck from HER centre rather than the visitor's, with the plainest paragraph on the site set beside it and her training printed as three entries in the margin key — no borrowed logos, no press, no client wall. (Name, years and training are UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 and ship as visibly-marked placeholders until the client confirms.)
staircaseBeats: Root — the summit, and the closest-set contours on the site: rings at 24px intervals over aura-two-people, enclosing three flat sentences, every ring visibly breaking around every line; the key in the margin reads clothed · no contact · no belief required.
Sacral — register change from drawing to plate: aura-light-in-a-room full-bleed, carrying only three rings at 180px intervals, one long near-voice paragraph in the widest band and no figures at all.

Solar plexus — register change to type as the structure: the four verbs at 96px, one per interval, each set flush-left in its own band with the ring opening around it — clearing, charging, repairing, restructuring, read outward from the centre.
Heart — register change to portrait and margin: her plate at half width with rings struck from her own centre, prose at 19px in one 62-character measure beside it, credentials as three key entries.

Throat — register change to the one region of the site with NO geometry on it at all: what this is not, set as plain ink on bare paper inside a ruled key box at the foot of the survey, the way a map states what it does not show. The absence of drawing is the detail that rewards attention.
Third eye — register change back to the drawing at its most open: two rings only, 400px apart, one named before-and-after paragraph in the band between them.

Products — register change to a schedule drawn onto the survey: courses, workshops and services at equal billing as three labelled bands at three radii, with real dates and prices in tabular figures set INSIDE the ring breaks — never in cards, never behind a filter.

Crown — the survey opens all the way out: one ring at the widest interval on the site encloses the whole viewport, the magenta-deep centre dot sits beneath the request, and the key is reprinted under it unchanged.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a woman who has been unable to decide for three weeks, because everything she reads is a promise and there is no way to check a promise. After: a woman who spent an hour in a chair with her coat on, who can tell you exactly what happened and exactly what did not, and who has stopped trying to work out whether to believe in it — because she has a description now instead of a claim. Nothing was cured. The guessing was.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The centre the rings have been tightening toward since the first screen is finally named at the Crown: it is the chair, and the person sitting in it is the visitor. The request sits on that centre, and the key printed beneath it is the same three lines the innermost ring enclosed — clothed, no contact, no belief required — so the page closes by repeating its opening measurement rather than by making a new promise.

interfaceCraftEmphasis: I-6 affordance legibility as a drawn convention she can learn in one sitting: everything interactive is enclosed by a ring that BREAKS for its own label, a disabled control's ring is closed and carries one line saying why, and the destructive confirmations (send to N confirmed subscribers; delete an offering three newsletters reference) are the only rings drawn in the error sienna.

I-3 scan hierarchy for a woman crossing her own kitchen: the admin dashboard's single most important datum — how many new requests, and which holds expire today — is set at 56px at the centre of the innermost ring and is readable from four feet away, before any list exists on the screen.

I-1 state-completeness drawn rather than blanked: the empty calendar, the zero-workshop index and the empty subscriber list are each a ring with one key entry and one control inside it, so day one of a brand-new practice reads as surveyed-and-currently-empty instead of as a broken page (brief §11's explicit day-one requirement).

I-5 density calibrated per screen rather than globally: the merged calendar is close-set, with contours tightening where the week is busy, while the landing-section editor is wide-interval and one field at a time — she reads her week fast and edits her copy slowly, and the drawing should know the difference.
excludes: NO STROKE MAY CROSS A GLYPH — the binding rule of this territory. Every ring, rule and arc terminates one em before a word's bounding box and resumes one em after it, and the break is genuinely drawn, never faked with a matching-colour rectangle over the line. A contour running through a paragraph or down a price column is a drafting error; it is the specific rendered failure of `the-mark-is-the-grid` that this child exists to correct.

No region enclosed by a ring may be empty. Every band carries prose, a plate, a key entry or a figure — a ring drawn around nothing is a dead field and gets cut before the composition ships. Negative space here is a measured interval, not a gap.
No type set on a curve, anywhere, ever. The rings are geometry and the words stay horizontal. Body 19px, secondary 17px, key entries and elevation figures 15px, and nothing on any surface below 14px.

No equally-spaced radial spokes, no compass rose, no mandala, no sacred geometry. The intervals are UNEQUAL and derived from each plate's own falloff, which is what makes this a measurement rather than an ornament — and ornament is precisely what the Carrier reads as 'you are being asked to believe something'.

Gold #E9C87E is barred from this paper outright at 1.36:1 — not 'non-text only', barred: it misses even the 3:1 SC 1.4.11 non-text floor here, so it cannot draw a ring, a rule, an edge or a focus state. Gold exists on this direction only INSIDE the photographs.
No card, no shadow, no rounded rectangle, no three-up service grid. Enclosure is a broken ring at a stated radius; there are no boxes anywhere on this site.
directions.layoutArchetype: A surveyed contour field printed on warm paper: measured concentric rings registered to the real centre of light inside each full-bleed plate, drawn at intervals that widen beat by beat, every ring breaking open around any word it meets so ink never touches a glyph; prose sits in the band between two rings, and a printed key holds the outer margin of every page.
directions.signatureMove: The broken contour ring — every rule, divider, enclosure and section edge on the site is an arc at a measured radius that TERMINATES a clear em before any glyph and resumes after it, cartographic convention, the line always yielding to the label. It is what lets the geometry run everywhere without ever crossing a word, and it reuses identically as the admin's enclosure, divider and focus primitive.
directions.toneRegister: cartographic warmth — hand-drawn accuracy on warm paper, nothing hidden and everything labelled
visualToneIndicators: the densest direction of the family — an 8px base on a compact 4/8/12/20/32/52 ramp, because a survey is legible by being close-set, not by being empty
sienna #9C3418 is the only ink that draws: rings, rules, key entries and the primary action are all the same colour, so the whole drawing reads as one hand
gold does not exist as ink on this paper at all — it lives only inside the photographs, which is exactly why the plates look lit and the page looks printed
one 8px magenta-deep dot at the true centre of every ring set: the person the field runs outward from. The only pure chroma on the page and the one detail that rewards a close look
elevation figures and key entries in IBM Plex Mono at 15px, set into the ring breaks — never smaller, because the reading glasses are somewhere else in the house
directions.theUnaskedQuestionAnswer: It is answered twice in the first viewport, in two different registers, and both are borrowed from map-making. The three facts are enclosed by the tightest contour on the entire site — the summit, the highest measured point — and the SAME three facts are reprinted as the map's key in the outer margin: clothed · no contact · no belief required. A key is a promise that nothing on the drawing is unexplained, which is the exact reassurance a sceptical adult needs before she reads a single claim.
directions.ascentMechanic: contour interval — the spacing between rings widens monotonically root to crown (24px at Root, 400px at Third Eye, one ring enclosing the viewport at Crown), so the survey opens out as the page climbs. Steep, close and urgent where the fear is; wide, open and quiet where the invitation is. inspirations.md §Four non-rainbow mechanics row 4 (density progression), realised as a drawn interval rather than as whitespace.

directions.name: the-lit-clearing
directions.governingIdea: The room is dark and there is one clearing of light in it the exact size of a seated person, and everything this site has to say is said from inside that clearing — while the practitioner's hands stay at its edge and never cross.
directions.singleMindedProposition: Nothing crosses this edge — not her hands, not a rule, not a line of type.

narrativeSpine.openWound: The thing you cannot ask is not whether it works. It is whether you will have to take your clothes off, and whether a stranger is going to put her hands on you, and you have closed four tabs this month at exactly the moment you understood that the page was never going to say.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: A woman is sitting in the light with her coat still on, and there is a pair of hands at the edge of it that have not come in. Four words underneath: nothing crosses this edge. Whose rule is that, and does it hold for the whole hour?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is the tab you close at 11:40pm — the category's habit of answering everything except the procedure, so the decision gets made by your embarrassment instead of by you. What it costs is another eight months of carrying the thing you arrived with, and calling that thinking about it.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She arrives at the fourth beat inside the smallest clearing on the site — close-cropped, at reading distance, her own plain sentences first and her training on one 15px line beneath, with no borrowed logos and no client wall. She is the person who drew the edge, and she says so plainly. (Name, years and training are UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 and ship as visibly-marked placeholders.)
staircaseBeats: Root — the clearing at the size of one seated person: aura-two-people full-bleed in near-black with the pool cut around the chair, three flat sentences and a four-word caption on the light. Dense and close: six elements in the pool.
Sacral — register change to a wide low pool over aura-light-in-a-room: five elements, one long paragraph at near-voice about what the hour is like from inside the chair, nothing else lit.

Solar plexus — register change to type as the entire content of the light: four verbs at 88px stacked in one pool with nothing else in it whatsoever — clearing, charging, repairing, restructuring — the plate visible all the way around them.
Heart — register change to the smallest clearing on the site: her face, one paragraph, one 15px line of training. Four elements.

Throat — register change AND an inversion: what this is not is the one beat set OUTSIDE the light, in blush type on the bare plate, with that beat's pool sitting empty beside it. The honesty is the one thing the light is not asked to carry, and it is the detail that rewards attention.
Third eye — register change back into a wide pool holding one named before-and-after paragraph and nothing else at all. Two elements.

Products — register change to a schedule on the light: three offering kinds at equal billing as rule-separated rows with real dates and prices in tabular figures, in the widest pool yet, still one column and still no cards.
Crown — the clearing has opened past all four edges and the page is light: one sentence, one control, two elements, and the plate survives only in the corners.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: someone who has had a practitioner's contact page open in another tab since March and has never scrolled it to the bottom, because she is waiting for a sentence that never comes. After: someone who spent an hour in a chair with her coat over the back of it, who can say exactly what happened and exactly what did not, and who found the whole thing considerably less strange than the version she had been imagining for six months. Nothing was cured. The bracing was.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The Crown answers the caption the first pool made. The hands never came in, the edge held for the whole hour, and the request now sits on open light with the same four words printed beneath it. What is being asked for is an hour in the clearing — not a belief, and not your clothes off.

interfaceCraftEmphasis: I-2 one primary action per screen made structural rather than stylistic: the clearing contains exactly ONE primary control, always, on every admin screen — so the answer to 'what do I do here' is permanently 'the thing in the light', and she learns it once and never relearns it.

I-4 progressive disclosure BY the edge, which is the lever that decides whether she can run this: the 80% path is whatever is lit, and everything rare — availability rules, publish scope, bulk actions, CSV export, hold duration — lives outside the pool at 15px and comes into the light on intent. It is how a nine-field settings screen stops looking like software to someone who is not comfortable with software (brief §6).

I-1 state-completeness with day one designed FIRST: the empty merged calendar, the zero-workshop index and the empty booking queue are each a clearing holding one sentence and one control, so a brand-new practice's admin looks composed rather than broken — brief §11's explicit requirement that a page with zero workshops is still worth landing on.

I-6 affordance legibility on a two-value system a non-technical owner can state out loud: anything on the light is operable, anything on the plate is information. The irreversible guards — send to N confirmed subscribers, delete an offering three newsletters reference — state the exact count and the exact consequence inside their own clearing, before the control rather than after it.
excludes: NOTHING CROSSES THE POOL'S BOUNDARY — the binding rule, and it is simultaneously the concept and the typographic fix. No rule, arc, stroke, divider or line of type may touch or span the edge; every element is wholly inside the light or wholly outside it, and type keeps a 32px clear band inside the boundary. Strokes and words never meet here because they never occupy the same region — which is the parent territory's arcs-through-paragraphs failure made structurally impossible.

No bare dark. Every pixel outside a clearing carries a plate at reduced luminance — the dark is photographic, always, everywhere. A flat black region is a failed render rather than restraint, and this territory has none on any screen including the admin.
No second clearing per viewport. Two pools cancel each other and the concept dies with them: one pool, and it is where the eye goes.

No scrim, tint or overlay laid over a plate to make type sit on it. If a word needs the picture darkened in order to be read, that word belongs in the clearing instead — which is what the clearing is for.

No drop shadow, no card, no rounded rectangle, no three-up grid. The edge of the light is the only boundary in the entire system, and adding a second kind of boundary would make the first one ordinary.

Body 18px inside the pool, 17px minimum anywhere, plate-side captions 15px and never smaller. Gold #E9C87E is barred INSIDE the pool (1.47:1) and magenta-deep #C2187A is barred OUTSIDE it (3.45:1) — each colour belongs to one side of the edge and crossing is a contrast failure as well as a concept failure.
directions.layoutArchetype: Near-black throughout, with one hard-edged clearing of blush light cut into a full-bleed plate per viewport; all reading happens on the light inside that clearing, the dark around it is never bare because it is always the photograph, and each beat the clearing holds fewer elements and more air than the beat before it.
directions.signatureMove: One hard-edged pool of blush light per viewport, cut clean out of a full-bleed plate, carrying every word and every control on the screen in plum ink — and nothing ever crosses its boundary: not a rule, not a stroke, not a line of type, and not the practitioner's hands, which enter the frame at the pool's edge in the plate and stop there. The pool reuses verbatim as the admin's panel, dialog, form and empty-state primitive.
directions.toneRegister: held clearing — near-black all around, and everything that matters read from inside one pool of light
visualToneIndicators: the sharpest edge in the family: the pool's boundary is a hard 1px transition with no feather, no glow and no falloff — this is a cut, not a bloom, and that is the whole difference from its dark parent

true light-on-dark inversion inside a dark world: the page ground is #160712 and reading happens on #FBF3F1 at 17.21:1, which is also the highest reading contrast available to a 35–65 audience anywhere in the set
the pool's element COUNT is the composition's unit — six at Root, two at Crown — so restraint is countable rather than a matter of taste

the one motion is the pool's edge drifting a few pixels on a ~14-second cycle, because a real pool of light in a real room is never perfectly still; under prefers-reduced-motion the edge sits at its beat's fixed position and the composition is whole
0px radius on everything that is not the pool; the pool is a true circle or a true rounded-rectangle clipped to the content it holds, never a decorative shape looking for something to contain
directions.theUnaskedQuestionAnswer: The composition answers it before a word is read, and the caption only names what is already visible. At Root the clearing is exactly the size of a seated, fully-clothed woman with her coat still on, and the practitioner's hands enter the frame at the pool's edge and STOP — visibly outside the light, in the plate. The three flat sentences sit on the light beside her, and the caption under the pool is four words: nothing crosses this edge. The picture and the sentence make the same claim simultaneously, so it survives a skim by someone who reads nothing.
directions.ascentMechanic: density / emptying — the clearing holds monotonically fewer elements and more air from Root (six) to Crown (two), so the climb is felt as things being taken away rather than as light being turned up. inspirations.md §Four non-rainbow mechanics row 4: 'Root is dense and close-set; crown is spacious and open'. No radius ramp and no luminance ramp — both belong to other territories.

directions.name: nothing-lit-from-the-front
directions.governingIdea: Every person, panel and control on this site is lit from behind at its edge and never from the front, because the fear this brand has to answer is the fear of being exposed — and a page where nothing is floodlit says that, before any sentence does.
directions.singleMindedProposition: You can see the shape of a person here without anything being exposed, and that is not a metaphor — it is how the page is lit.

narrativeSpine.openWound: What actually stops you is not doubt, it is the picture in your head of standing in a bright room in a paper gown while a stranger looks at you — and because that picture is embarrassing, you have never typed the question, so you have spent four months deciding on the basis of an image you invented yourself.
narrativeSpine.openLoop: The first screen is a person whose whole shape you can see and none of whose detail you can: lit from behind, coat on, face in shadow. There is a thin line of light along one edge. It is clearly travelling. Where does it end up?
narrativeSpine.villainStakes: The villain is exposure — the assumption running through this entire category that being helped means being looked at. It wins by never once being contradicted, and it costs this practice the exact person it exists for: the adult who half-expects to be embarrassed and leaves before finding out that she would not have been.
narrativeSpine.guideEntrance: She enters at the fourth beat lit exactly the way the visitor is — her own portrait rim-lit with her face in shadow, her plain sentences at 19px beside it, her training on one 15px line beneath. The guide stands under the same lighting as the hero, which is the entire point: nobody on this site is floodlit, including her. (Name, years and training are UNVERIFIED per brief §20.1 and ship as visibly-marked placeholders.)
staircaseBeats: Root — the thinnest crescent on the site: aura-two-people inside a 520px disc lit along one edge only, three facts at 44px flush-left beside it, and a caption naming the lighting itself — nothing here is lit from the front.
Sacral — register change to a wide low disc at 1100px with the light now a quarter of the way round, one long near-voice paragraph at 19px about what the hour is actually like, set beside it.

Solar plexus — register change to display type carrying the beat alone: the four verbs at 104px in four stacked flush-left lines, each with its own small disc at a further phase to its left — clearing, charging, repairing, restructuring — the only place on the site where the rim appears four times at once.
Heart — register change to portrait: her disc at 640px with the light halfway round, prose in a single 60-character measure beside it, credentials at 15px.

Throat — register change to the one screen with NO disc and NO rim at all: what this is not, set as plain blush prose on bare dusk, edge-lit only by a single coral hairline the width of the measure. The beat where nothing is lit is the detail that rewards attention.
Third eye — register change back to a disc at three-quarter rim, one named before-and-after paragraph beside it and nothing else on the screen.

Products — register change to a lit schedule: the three offering kinds at equal billing as rule-separated rows whose left edges are lit to the phase of the beat, with real dates and prices in tabular figures — no cards, no disc, no filter.

Crown — the light has come all the way round: the first and only complete rim on the site, aura-radiant-portrait inside it, one sentence and one control, and that control is the one other element with a complete rim of its own.
narrativeSpine.transformationBridge: Before: a woman who has been picturing a bright room and a paper gown for four months and has therefore never gone, and who could not tell a single person that this is what stopped her. After: a woman who sat in a low-lit room in her own clothes for an hour with nobody's hands on her, who now knows the picture in her head was of a completely different appointment, and who books the next one without thinking about it. Nothing was cured. The picture was replaced with a memory.
narrativeSpine.closedLoop: The line of light that began as a crescent on the first screen closes into a complete ring at the Crown, and the request sits inside it. What the rim was travelling toward turns out to be the invitation — and nothing along the way, including the invitation, was ever lit from the front.

interfaceCraftEmphasis: I-6 affordance legibility carried entirely by the rim, which is the lever that decides whether she can run her business on this: a COMPLETE coral rim is the one primary action on the screen, a partial rim is secondary, an unlit rim is disabled and carries a one-line reason — and the guarded destructive actions (send to N confirmed subscribers; delete an offering that three newsletters reference) are rimmed in the error hue at 8.41:1 and state the count BEFORE the control, not after it.

I-5 density done right on the screen she will live in: the merged calendar separates confirmed bookings, pending holds, derived session blocks and personal blocks by four RIM treatments with no fills competing anywhere on the grid, so a densely-booked week stays readable and free time stays legible as free. This is the Tufte case exactly — on this ground a fill would be the only thing on the grid with any weight, and it would win against the data.

I-3 scan hierarchy for a non-technical owner who opens her admin once a month: the dashboard answers 'what needs me today' in a single rim-lit block at 44px — new requests, and holds about to expire — before any table exists on the screen at all.

I-2 one primary action per screen with a mechanical test rather than a taste judgement: count the complete rims. If there is more than one on a screen, the hierarchy has failed and one of them gets demoted to a partial.

I-1 state-completeness with the empty states composed FIRST: an empty week, a zero-workshop index and an empty subscriber list are a rim with one sentence inside it — a shape, not an absence — which is brief §11's day-one requirement met by composition rather than by an apology.
excludes: NOTHING IS LIT FROM THE FRONT. There is not one solid button, filled card, white panel or filled chip anywhere in the system — separation is a lit EDGE, always, and a single filled rectangle would break the whole grammar in one element. The only exception is a plate, which is a photograph and carries its own light.

NO STROKE CROSSES A WORD. A rim belongs to an OBJECT and closes on that object's own edge; type sits inside an object or beside it, never across a rim, and no rule, arc or divider is ever drawn through a text block or down a price column. The parent territory's arcs running through paragraphs is the exact failure this clause exists to make impossible.

No moon phases, no crescent as a decorative motif, no astrology, no mandala, no sacred geometry. The travelling rim is PHOTOGRAPHIC backlight — what a portrait photographer does to give a subject an edge without exposing a face — and the moment it reads as lunar this brand has walked back into the category it is leaving.

No condensed display face and no flat acid accent on this ground: Othership ships exactly that combination at #372338 and this ground sits one measured step from it. Bricolage Grotesque runs at normal or wide width only, never condensed.

No dead dusk. Any region without content carries a plate at reduced luminance or one edge-lit hairline; a flat expanse of plum with nothing in it is a failed render and gets composed or cut. Negative space here is a lit interval, not an absence.
Body 18px, secondary 17px, captions and figures 15px, nothing below 14px on any surface including the admin — the audience skews 35–65 and the reading glasses are somewhere else in the house.

Magenta #D6338A (3.58:1) and magenta-deep #C2187A (2.82:1) are barred on this ground outright; magenta-deep misses even the 3:1 non-text floor here, which is the README's own dark-ground warning made binding rather than advisory.
directions.layoutArchetype: Dusk plum held at one value across the whole site, with objects separated from the ground by a lit edge instead of by a fill: one large disc carries the image on each beat, its bright rim running further around the circumference at every step of the climb, and display lines stack flush-left beside it at full measure with no type ever set on a curve.
directions.signatureMove: Rim light as the entire elevation and affordance currency: nothing is filled and nothing is floodlit, every disc, panel, field and control is separated from the dusk by a coral edge-light, and how far that light has travelled around an object's circumference is what tells you what the object is — a complete rim is the one primary action, a partial rim is secondary, an unlit rim is disabled and says why.
directions.toneRegister: rim-lit reserve — lit from behind, never from the front, and warm at every edge
visualToneIndicators: surfaces differ from the ground by 1.04:1 and are separated ENTIRELY by their lit edge at 6.53:1 — the palette itself refuses front-lighting, and the separation still clears the 3:1 non-text floor twice over

one continuous ground value from the header to the footer of every page, public and admin: dusk plum #3A1233, the brand's own third plum, used as a ground by nothing else in the set

the one motion is the rim's brightest point travelling a few degrees on a ~16-second cycle; under prefers-reduced-motion it sits at that beat's fixed phase and the composition is whole and still legible as a step in the climb
coral #F5876F rather than gold as the light, because gold on plum is the parent's colour and coral is warmer, more photographic and reads as a real backlight rather than as a metal
directions.theUnaskedQuestionAnswer: The LIGHTING answers it before the copy gets a chance. Every figure on this site is edge-lit and clothed with the face in soft shadow, and no plate anywhere is lit from the front — so the visitor's own invented picture of a bright room and a paper gown is contradicted by the first thing on the screen. Beside that first thin crescent the three facts are set at 44px in blush: you stay dressed, nobody touches you, nothing is asked of your beliefs. The caption names the mechanism rather than the reassurance — nothing here is lit from the front — which is a more credible thing to say than 'don't worry'.
directions.ascentMechanic: angular travel — the arc of lit rim runs further around the disc at each beat, from a thin crescent at Root to the first and only complete ring at Crown. No radius change, no luminance ramp, no hue rotation and no density ramp: the climb is measured in degrees, which is a mechanic nothing else in the set uses.

derivedStyle.characteristics: Zero fills and zero shadows anywhere — every boundary is a 1.5px edge-light at partial or complete arc; surface differs from ground by 1.04:1 on purpose so the rim does all the separating; body 18px / 1.7; the four verbs at 104px are the largest type in the family.
derivedStyle.ground: dusk plum #3A1233 — the brand's own plum-700, one measured step lighter and warmer than the parent's midnight #2B0E28, and used as a page ground by no other direction in the set. Dusk rather than midnight, which is what lets a coral rim read as backlight instead of as neon.
derivedStyle.gradientRole: EDGE ONLY. The gold→magenta gradient appears solely as the falloff along an object's lit rim — coral at the brightest point of the arc easing to gold at its tail — so the brand's gradient is expressed as a light source's temperature rather than as a fill, a swatch, or a background wash.
